warmup.text: Before you read, a famous poem full of words that don't exist, and yet you can almost understand them. Listen to the sounds. Then think: why is nonsense funny?

words.text: Find rid, ris, lud and lus in new words. Then look at speech spellings, where an apostrophe takes the place of a missing letter. In the game, six more narrows. Two of them test speech spellings.

reading.text: Read Chapter 5, Land of Fire. The storms are fierce. Watch what Praiseworthy says out loud, and what the narrator tells you he really believes. Then watch for the surprise at the end of the chapter.

assignment.text: Three questions about Chapter 5. Then keep drafting your scene. Give one character a line of dialogue and a reaction that shows how they feel. Use the frames if you get stuck.

ris: It is the laugh root that ends in s.
lu: Two letters of the play root.
lude: To slip away, as in a game.
The play root, plus a silent e.
rid: The laugh root that ends in d.

game.title: Through the Strait
game.sub: This week's word game · 6 narrows today
game.look: Your ship sails west through the Strait of Magellan, a narrow passage at the bottom of South America. At each narrows, tap the channel with the word that really fits. Each narrows you pass lights a fire on Tierra del Fuego, the Land of Fire.

do: Read the clue at the narrows.
Look at the word in each channel.
Tap the channel with the word that really fits.
Tap Sail on.
how.why: A root only helps if it is really there, and a speech spelling only works if the apostrophe is in the right place.

game.doneLine: The Pacific is open. Come back tomorrow for six more narrows.

narrows.clue: Find the word with lud (play): to trick someone into believing something false.
narrows.why: de + lud: to play someone false. Deliver comes from liber, which means free.

narrows.clue: Find the word with lud (play): to hint at something without saying it straight out.
narrows.why: al (toward) + lud (play): to play toward an idea. Allow has no play root.

narrows.clue: Which word carries rid (laugh) and means so silly it deserves a laugh?
narrows.why: rid + iculous: worth laughing at. Rigorous means strict and careful; it has no laugh root.
de + ris + ive: full of mocking laughter. A rider rides; the r-i-d is just letters.
narrows.miss: Does rider have anything to do with laughing?

narrows.clue: Chapter 4: Mountain Jim says a boy needs all the schooling he can get. Which spelling is his?
narrows.why: educatin' = educating. The apostrophe goes where the g was, at the end.

narrows.clue: Chapter 1: a gold-seeker pushing toward the stove calls someone partner. Which spelling shows how he says it?
narrows.why: pardner is how he says partner. No letter is missing, just a sound changed, so there is no apostrophe.
narrows.miss: Is a letter really left out here, or just changed?

cards.title: Real history: the Strait of Magellan
cards.intro: The Lady Wilma and the Sea Raven are made up. The places in Chapter 5 are real.

items.meaning: A narrow, twisting passage of water between the tip of South America and the islands south of it. It is about 350 miles long and from 2 to 20 miles wide. In 1520 Ferdinand Magellan's ships became the first European ships to sail through it.

Spanish for Land of Fire. Magellan's crew saw the fires of the people who lived there and named the land for them. The Selk'nam, Yaghan, Kaweskar and Haush peoples had lived there for thousands of years.

items.term: A real steamship took this route
items.meaning: The paddle steamer SS California left New York in October 1848. She stopped at Rio de Janeiro, steamed through the Strait of Magellan, stopped at Callao in Peru, and reached San Francisco on February 28, 1849, the first steamship to arrive there in the Gold Rush.

cards.note: Sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica; the Maritime Heritage Project (San Francisco ship arrivals, 1849).

virtue.name: self-control

options.t: Praiseworthy calls the scary sea stories “Stuff and nonsense,” even though he believes every word of them.
Holding onto a post with the hook of his umbrella, Praiseworthy calls the storm “A mere squall.”
In the boiler room, the butler seems unafraid, and Jack finds comfort in being at his side.

virtue.line: Tap the moment that shows the most self-control. Then tell why in one sentence.

art.title: H.M.S. Beagle in the Straits of Magellan
art.alt: A black-and-white engraving of a three-masted sailing ship in a narrow channel between steep dark hills, a snowy peak behind, and people paddling small canoes nearby.
art.look: The Beagle was a real British survey ship that mapped the Strait of Magellan in the 1820s and 1830s, with a young Charles Darwin aboard on its second voyage. This engraving was made in 1890. Mount Sarmiento stands in the distance, and Native people paddle canoes near the ship. The Lady Wilma is made up; the strait is real.
